hird.name: Hirdman
hird.prompt:
Fantasy trading-card illustration in the style of early-to-mid 1990s card art: hand-made traditional media (gouache, acrylic, watercolour and pen-and-ink), visible brushstrokes and pen lines, matte paper texture, and the slightly soft, faded look of a card printed in the 1990s. Expressive and a little stylised rather than realistic: strong shapes, bold silhouettes, sometimes inked outlines and flat patterned colour. Dark overall with near-black shadows, lit by bold, saturated accent colours taken from the card's own light and colour key (no default orange) where they matter. Frame the subject tightly: it fills most of the picture and may be cropped by the edges, with its face or focal point near the centre; keep the background minimal, simple and dark. Landscape 3:2 composition. No text, no letters, no border, no card frame, no logo, no watermark, no signature. Not photorealistic, not 3D render, not modern digital concept art, not anime.

Norse look for this hero: the same 1990s hand-made card art, but colder and harder than the Greek cards. A wide background illustration for the battle screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain clearly showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour. A limited palette of 4 or 5 colours, dark overall. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting, no glow, no soft gradients, no depth of field, no fine detail or texture rendering, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art. Composition for a game board: low contrast, all the interesting shapes at the edges and in the bottom corners; the centre is a calm, empty, evenly dark area, because game cards sit on top of it. No figures or creatures in the centre. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no logo, no signature.

Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain clearly showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour. A limited palette of 4 or 5 colours, dark overall. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting, no glow, no soft gradients, no depth of field, no fine detail or texture rendering, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art. Composition for a game board: low contrast, all the interesting shapes at the edges and in the bottom corners; the centre is a calm, empty, evenly dark area, because game cards sit on top of it. No figures or creatures in the centre. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no logo, no signature.

Setting: the Palm Cloud Cave of the Bull Demon King from Journey to the West, at the foot of the Flaming Mountains: a demon king's cavern palace with huge black-iron doors studded with bosses at the far left; enormous bull horns mounted over a throne of red rock; his giant iron cudgel leaning against a pillar at the lower right; the Flaming Mountains blazing on the horizon through the cave mouth; smoke and ash drifting The brush rhythm of Chinese ink-wash painting mixed into the pen-and-ink style. Distinctly Chinese: no Japanese, Greek or Norse elements.
Colour: near-black iron to deep red (#140808 to #7a2a1e) with bronze, flame orange and dull gold accents.
